newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: More violence rocks Pakistan as 21 die in mosque.
newsitem.headline: More violence rocks Pakistan as 21 die in mosque.

text.p: More violence erupted in Pakistan on Monday as gunmen killed 21 worshippers at a Sunni Moslem mosque and police fired at demonstrators loyal to the slain brother of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto.

Four men sprayed gunfire at a mosque in the central city of Multan, killing 21 people and wounding many more, ambulance workers said. Many of the casualties were boys studying at a religious school attached to the mosque.

The shooting, which followed the murder on Sunday of a Shi'ite Moslem leader in Bahawalpur, about 95 km (60 miles) south of Multan, was the latest in a vicious feud between militant groups in Pakistan's minority Shi'ite and majority Sunni communities.
Angry crowds later took to the streets, beating policemen, stoning Shi'ite neighbourhoods, blocking roads with burning tyres and shouting anti-Shi'ite slogans, witnesses said.
The sectarian violence coincided with trouble in Bhutto's home town of Larkana, where police fought followers of her estranged brother Murtaza, killed by Karachi police on Friday in a gunbattle.
Witnesses said two people were wounded when police fired bullets and teargas to disperse several hundred protesters near Murtaza's home on the last day of official mourning.
Sources in his breakaway faction of the ruling Pakistan People's Party (PPP), known as PPP-Shaheed Bhutto, said one protester had been killed, but this could not be confirmed.
The prime minister and her mother, Nusrat Bhutto, planned to leave Larkana for Karachi later on Monday to receive condolences there.
Murtaza's Lebanese widow Ghinwa was expected to fly separately to the southern port city.
The PPP-Shaheed Bhutto faction invited Ghinwa to become its leader, but party sources said she was unlikely to declare her intentions until a 40-day Moslem mourning period was over.

Murtaza's faction issued a statement on Monday accusing police of shooting their leader and 11 of his followers in an ambush and delaying the transfer of the dead and wounded to a hospital, which was inadequately equipped to cope with the casualties.
Police say they fired in self-defence after Murtaza's bodyguards began shooting to prevent police checks.

Opposition politicians and newspapers criticised police for being trigger-happy and undisciplined. Karachi police were in action again on Monday, shooting dead five armed robbers who failed to inflict any casualties in the clash, police said.
Murtaza's killing has bereaved the powerful, but unfortunate, Bhutto clan for a third time in two decades.

Benazir's father, former prime minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, was hanged in 1979 by former military ruler General Mohammad Zia-ul-Haq, who deposed him in 1977. Her younger brother Shahnawaz died, apparently poisoned, in France in 1985.
